title: Springs in CSS, Styled CSV, Scriptless Typing, Click Bursts & Scroll-Snap Sheets
description: Five patterns that push the behaviour out of a script and into something the browser already runs.

drops.title: Motion You Declare, Not Script
drops.description: Cards tilt, layers lift on the parent's own z axis and a dock magnifies — all of it stated as custom properties.
drops.concept: Kinesis registers --k-* custom properties so the browser computes them first, then hands the result to a spring. The element never knows about a pointer; it only declares how far it is willing to lean, and five stiffness/damping presets decide how it gets there and how it settles.

interaction.mouse: Move across the deck — each card springs toward the pointer and its layers parallax apart; pass the dock to magnify icons by proximity
interaction.click: Pick a motion preset to change stiffness and damping, or drag the tilt, depth and magnify sliders
interaction.touch: Drag anywhere over the cards; the panel moves inline under the header on narrow screens

drops.title: The Stylesheet Lives in the Data
drops.description: A CSS block fenced by --- sitting on top of ordinary CSV, in one plain-text file that the browser renders as a styled table.
drops.concept: Delete the fenced block and you still have a valid spreadsheet export; keep it and a custom element splits the file, sandboxes the rules in a shadow root and builds the table. Rows are addressable by key via --cssv-key, and numeric cells carry their value as --n, so a heat map needs no JavaScript at all.

interaction.mouse: Edit either half of the file and the table re-renders as you type; errors report instead of blanking the pane
interaction.click: Four example files — a ledger with a keyed total row, a roster, plain CSV with no style block, and a pure-CSS heat map
interaction.touch: Panes stack vertically; the editor stays a real textarea

drops.title: A Typewriter With No Script
drops.description: Glyphs are a ::before whose width steps across whole ch units; the caret is an ::after on its own blink track.
drops.concept: The keyframe percentages are the entire program — type, hold, delete, hold — and steps() makes the width land on character boundaries so it never shows half a glyph. Three strings share one grid cell on a slot track, and a flat stretch mid-keyframe makes a line hesitate exactly where you want it.

interaction.mouse: Nothing to hover — the animation is the page; sliders retune it live
interaction.click: Drag cycle, caret blink and caret width; flip play to paused to freeze every track at once
interaction.touch: Panel moves inline; prefers-reduced-motion shows the finished strings with no animation

drops.title: Every Click Gets an Answer
drops.description: A dissolving ring, a core that flashes and collapses, a spray of rotating slivers — then a trail that shortens from its own tail.
drops.concept: Three layers run on one clock per burst, each with its own size and opacity curve, composited additively so overlaps bloom. The trail is the interesting half: points carry timestamps and are dropped from the tail, so the stroke visibly gets shorter along its path instead of fading as a whole.

interaction.mouse: Click anywhere to fire a burst; hold and drag to draw a trail that shortens behind you
interaction.click: Tune scale, bloom and time scale, pick one of four theme colours, or switch the trail between press-only and always
interaction.touch: Taps and drags both work; the panel docks to the bottom on narrow screens

drops.title: The Sheet Is the Scroller
drops.description: A bottom sheet with no drag handlers: the detents are scroll-snap targets, so flinging it is plain scrolling.
drops.concept: Zero-height markers inside a scroll container carry scroll-snap-align, so the platform's own snapping picks the resting detent with the platform's own momentum curve. The backdrop fades on a scroll() timeline, and the sheet's content scroll and the sheet gesture are literally the same scroll.

interaction.mouse: Wheel over the sheet to move it; let go anywhere and it snaps to the nearest detent. Click the dimmed area above it to dismiss
interaction.click: Jump to peek, half or full from the detent panel; Escape closes
interaction.touch: Fling the grip — it is an ordinary scroll, so it inherits native momentum and rubber-banding
